_sources.12: TY2025 standard deduction, married filing jointly: base $31,500 (Rev. Proc. 2024-40 as adjusted by OBBBA, P.L. 119-21) PLUS the additional amount for age 65: both spouses are 65 or older at the end of 2025 (taxpayer born 1958-05-01, spouse born 1960-11-15; a taxpayer born before January 2, 1961 is considered 65 - Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), Standard Deduction, and the date is printed on the form). Additional amount per condition for a married taxpayer is $1,600 (Rev. Proc. 2024-40; IR-2024-273), and there are 2 conditions (taxpayer age, spouse age; neither is blind), so $31,500 + 2 x $1,600 = $34,700; Form 1040 line 12 (printed as 12e)

description: Married filing jointly; one W-2 ($70,000 wages, $6,000 withheld); identity block stored with both spouses age 65+ (DOBs 1958-05-01 and 1960-11-15, both born before January 2, 1961) with SSNs, neither blind. Line 12 = $31,500 base + 2 x $1,600 age additions = $34,700. Both spouses also take the Schedule 1-A Part V enhanced deduction for seniors (MAGI $70,000 is under the $150,000 phaseout threshold): line 13b = $12,000, line 14 = $46,700, taxable income $23,300. Money values below are integer cents.
